description: Chapter summaries the reader shows under a chapter's title, keyed by chapter number, per language. Like section headings they are editorial aids, not translation: written from Open Word Bible's own wording, stating what the chapter is about and nothing more, so every language can say the same thing. They use no reader settings. Every summary is an AI draft until a named reviewer approves it.

1.en: The Teacher declares that everything is a breath. Generations come and go, the world repeats itself, and the pursuit of wisdom only brings sorrow.

2.en: The Teacher tries pleasure, great works and wealth and finds them all a breath. Wise and foolish both die, and the best a person can do is to enjoy eating, drinking and work as gifts from God.

3.en: There is a time for everything under heaven. God has set eternity in the human heart, and people should enjoy their work, for humans and animals alike return to dust.

4.en: The Teacher sees oppression and envy, and finds that two are better than one. A poor but wise youth is better than an old and foolish king.

5.en: People should approach God with few words and keep their vows. Wealth never satisfies, and the ability to enjoy what one has is God's gift.

6.en: A person may have wealth and long life yet not enjoy them. No one knows what is good for a person in life.

7.en: A good name is better than perfume, and wisdom gives strength. The Teacher finds that God made people upright, but they have sought out many schemes.

8.en: People should obey the king, though no one knows what is to come. The righteous and the wicked do not always receive what they deserve, so the Teacher commends enjoyment of life.

9.en: The same fate comes to all, so people should enjoy their bread and wine and their life with the one they love. Wisdom is better than strength, though it is often ignored.

10.en: A little folly outweighs wisdom, and the proverbs warn against foolish words, lazy rulers and careless work.

11.en: People should cast their bread on the waters and sow their seed, for they do not know what will prosper. The young should enjoy their youth, knowing that God will judge.

12.en: People should remember their Creator in their youth, before old age and death. The Teacher's conclusion is to fear God and keep God's commands, for God will judge every deed.
